title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #01
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #01 · Q1
items.stem:
Match the following :
I. Kingsley Amis — 1. Saturday and Sunday Morning
II. Allan Sillitoe — 2. The Golden Note Book
III. Doris Lessing — 3. The Left Bank
IV. Jean Rhys — 4. Lucky Jim
The correct combination according to the code is :
Codes : I II III IV
items.explanation: Kingsley Amis wrote Lucky Jim (I-4), Alan Sillitoe wrote Saturday Night and Sunday Morning (II-1), Doris Lessing wrote The Golden Notebook (III-2), and Jean Rhys wrote The Left Bank and Other Stories (IV-3).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q2
items.stem:
During the years 1830 to 1850, the illusion of peace in Victorian England was broken by such
incidents as ___________
options: the disaster of the Indian Mutiny and the incompetent bungling of the Crimean War
General Strike of 1835 and the Rail Tragedy of 1847
the visionary libertarianism of poets and the lawless embodiment of revolution
Revolution in France and the Chartist Movement in England
items.explanation: Between 1830 and 1850 (the 'Hungry Forties'), Victorian England's domestic peace was shaken by the working-class agitation of the Chartist Movement (1838–1848) at home and the revolutionary upheavals of the 1830 and 1848 Revolutions in France and continental Europe.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q3
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are correct about Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s “Annihilation of Caste” and concerns dealt within it?
A. It is an undelivered speech written in 1936.
B. It focuses on the need to create a society where individuals are treated with dignity, respect, regardless of their caste.
C. There will be outcastes even if the caste system is completely destroyed.
D. Ideal society will always have a strong caste system even if it is based on liberty, equality and fraternity.
E. This is a fictitious novel.
items.explanation: Annihilation of Caste was originally drafted in 1936 as an undelivered presidential address for the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal conference in Lahore before Ambedkar self-published it as a treatise (A). Ambedkar observed that outcaste status and social exclusion persist in social attitudes even when formal structural caste divisions are nominally challenged (C). Statements D and E are false because Ambedkar advocated the total abolition of caste and the work is a non-fictional socio-political treatise.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q4
items.stem: In how many volumes George Eliot’s Middlemarch was first published?
items.explanation: George Eliot's *Middlemarch, A Study of Provincial Life* was first published by William Blackwood in eight separate bimonthly paperback parts (volumes) between December 1871 and December 1872.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q5
items.stem: Which arrangement of D.H. Lawrence's novels is in the correct chronological sequence?
options: Kangaroo — The Plumed Serpent — Sons and Lovers — The Rainbow
Sons and Lovers — The Rainbow — Kangaroo — The Plumed Serpent
The Rainbow — The Plumed Serpent — Kangaroo — Sons and Lovers
The Rainbow — Kangaroo — The Plumed Serpent — Sons and Lovers
items.explanation: The correct chronological sequence of D. H. Lawrence's novels by publication year is: Sons and Lovers (1913), The Rainbow (1915), Kangaroo (1923), and The Plumed Serpent (1926).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q6
items.stem:
Where ignorance is Bliss

Tis folly to be wise." Who wrote the
following lines ?
items.explanation: These famous concluding lines come from Thomas Gray's poem Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College (1747), where the speaker reflects that carefree schoolboys should not be burdened prematurely with knowledge of adult sorrow.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q7
items.stem: "The great English novelists are Jane Austen, George Eliot, Henry James and Joseph Conrad." Which one of the following critical texts begins with the above assertion?
options: F. R. Leavis, The Great Tradition
Ian Watt, Rise of the Novel
items.explanation: This is the opening sentence of F. R. Leavis's 'The Great Tradition' (1948).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q8
items.stem:
Whom
does
Alexander
Pope
satirise in the portrait of Sporus ?
items.explanation: In An Epistle to Dr. Arbuthnot (1735), Alexander Pope viciously satirizes the Whig courtier and memoirist John Hervey, 2nd Baron Hervey, under the portrait of 'Sporus,' mocking him as a 'painted child of dirt, that stinks and stings.'

items.title: Mock #01 · Q9
items.stem:
Which of the following are applicable to the term 'Carnival'?
A. It became important through the work of the Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin.
B. It means the way in which popular humour subverts official authority in classical, medieval and renaissance texts and culture.
C. It overturns the established hierarchy and sets up a popular and democratic counter-culture.
D. It brings out the serious elements in literature.
E. It is used as a critical tool for interpretation of poetry.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The concept of the 'carnivalesque' was developed by Russian theorist Mikhail Bakhtin in Rabelais and His World (A) to describe how folk humor and grotesque realism subvert official authority (B) and temporarily overturn social hierarchies to create an egalitarian counter-culture (C).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q10
items.stem:
Pinter once admitted that he first became aware of the dramatic power of the pause from
seeing a popular American comedian.  Which one ?
items.explanation: Playwright Harold Pinter acknowledged that he first recognized the dramatic power and tension of the well-timed silence—later famous as the 'Pinter pause'—from watching the comedic timing of American entertainer Jack Benny.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q11
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I
List II
(Book)                                      (Poet)
A. Anniversaries
I. Abraham Cowley
B. The Temple
II. John Donne
C. The Rehearsal Transpros'dIII. George Herbert
D. Pindarique Odes
IV. Andrew Marvell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The Anniversaries (1611–12) were written by John Donne (A-II), The Temple (1633) by George Herbert (B-III), the prose satire The Rehearsal Transpros'd (1672–73) by Andrew Marvell (C-IV), and Pindarique Odes (1656) by Abraham Cowley (D-I).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q12
items.stem: In “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner” what disaster befalls the ship and the crew ?
options: The ship is becalmed and the crew dies of thirst.
A fierce storm batters the ship and drowns the crew.
“Slimy things with legs” attack the ship and kill many of the crew.
The ship is caught in ice and breaks into pieces.
items.explanation: After the Mariner shoots the Albatross in Coleridge's 'The Rime of the Ancient Mariner', the ship enters the doldrums and is becalmed under a burning sun, causing all two hundred sailors to perish agonizingly of thirst.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q13
items.meta: Unit X: Research Methods and Materials in English
items.stem:
An ideal research paper should include:
A. A statement that establishes the problem or controversial issue that the paper intends to examine.
B. Background information to establish past theories and current ideas on the topic.
C. Summarizing and paraphrasing.
D. Glorification of the paper writer himself.
E. A thesis to establish one’s position.
items.explanation: A sound academic research paper requires a clear statement of the research problem or question (A), sufficient literature review and background context to frame current scholarly debates (B), and a clear, argumentative thesis statement establishing the author's claim (E). Self-glorification (D) violates scholarly objectivity, while summarization (C) is merely a supporting technique rather than a foundational requirement.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q14
items.stem: In Pinter's Birthday Party, Stanley is given a birthday present. What is it ?
items.explanation: In Act I of Harold Pinter's comedy of menace The Birthday Party (1958), Meg and Lulu present the reclusive former pianist Stanley Webber with a boy's toy drum and drumsticks as a birthday gift, which he beats with growing frenzy and terror as the act ends.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q15
items.stem:
Arrange the following texts of critical theory in the correct chronological order of their publication.
A. Michel Foucault's The Archaeology of Knowledge
B. Roland Barthes' Mythologies
C. Jacques Derrida's Of Grammatology
D. Jacques Lacan's Ecrits
E. Jean-Francois Lyotard's The Postmodern Condition: A Report on Knowledge
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Dates: Barthes' Mythologies (1957), Lacan's Ecrits (1966), Derrida's Of Grammatology (1967), Foucault's Archaeology of Knowledge (1969), Lyotard's Postmodern Condition (1979). So the order is B, D, C, A, E.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q16
items.stem: Which writer applied the term 'cultural poetics' to his own critical contribution to make literature and arts as part of social practice?
items.explanation: Greenblatt preferred 'cultural poetics' to 'New Historicism' for his method of reading literature within social practice.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: Language is not a reliable tool of communication, says deconstruction, but argues in favour of a theory of sign
as a self-sufficient union of signifier and signified.
Statement II: Deconstruction claims that language is non-referential since it refers neither to the things in the world nor to
our concepts of things but only to the play of signifiers.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
items.explanation: Statement I is incorrect because Jacques Derrida and deconstruction dismantle Saussure's stable union of signifier and signified; Statement II is correct because deconstruction views language as an endless differential play of signifiers (différance).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q18
items.stem: In whose poem the readers meet Aunt Jennifer's tigers?
items.explanation: 'Aunt Jennifer's Tigers' (1951) is an early feminist poem by American poet Adrienne Rich (from her debut collection A Change of World), contrasting a married woman's domestic oppression under 'the massive weight of Uncle's wedding band' with the fearless, prancing tigers she embroiders.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q19
items.stem:
Which of the following option(s) cover the basic issues related to feminist literary criticism?

A. Women are caught up in a prison house of language that is male specific

B. Gender equality is just an idea and largely unachievable

C. Human society is largely entrenched in patriarchal ideology

D. Sex and Gender can not be treated as two distinct categories

E. One universal feminism will be the remedy to the historical subjugation

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Statements A and C represent fundamental concerns of feminist literary criticism: analyzing how women are trapped within a male-centered linguistic and symbolic order, and critiquing how literary traditions and societal institutions are entrenched in patriarchal ideology. In contrast, feminist criticism insists that sex and gender are distinct categories (D is false) and rejects any monolithic, single universal feminism (E is false).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q20
items.stem:
"When nature prompted and no law denied
Promiscuous use of concubine and bride;
Then Israel's monarch after Heaven's own heart,
His vigorous warmth did variously impart
To wives and slaves."
From which poem are these lines taken?
options: A Song for St. Cecilia's Day
items.explanation: These lines are the famous opening verses (lines 5–9) of John Dryden's Biblical-political satire Absalom and Achitophel: A Poem (1681), which allegorizes King Charles II as King David ('Israel's monarch') and the Earl of Shaftesbury as Achitophel during the Exclusion Crisis.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q21
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Poets)
(A) Purushottam Lal
(B) Adil Jussawalla
(C) A. K. Ramanujan
(D) R. Parthasarathy

List II (Poetry Collections)
(I) The Striders
(II) The Parrot's Death and Other Poems
(III) Rough Passage
(IV) Missing Person

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: P. Lal published The Parrot's Death and Other Poems (1960, A-II); Adil Jussawalla published Missing Person (1976, B-IV); A. K. Ramanujan published The Striders (1966, C-I); and R. Parthasarathy published Rough Passage (1977, D-III).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q22
items.stem:
“The Gilded Age” refers to a period of American history between 1870 and the first decades
of the twentieth century.
Who among the following American writers is credited with the coining of the term ?
items.explanation: Mark Twain and Charles Dudley Warner coined 'The Gilded Age' as the title of their collaborative 1873 satirical novel, mocking post-Civil War American society as covered with a glittering golden veneer that hid rampant political corruption and greed.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q23
items.stem:
Ralph Ellison enjoys subverting myths
about white purity through characters like :

(a)
Norton
(b) Bledsoe

(c)
Rhinehart
(d) all of the above
items.explanation: In the early chapters of Ralph Ellison's novel Invisible Man (1952), myths of white purity and philanthropic paternalism are subverted through the white millionaire trustee Mr. Norton (whose idealized fixation on his daughter masks incestuous desires) and the manipulative Black college president Dr. Bledsoe (a and b).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q24
items.stem: Patrick White’s classic work Voss is based on the story of a …………… explorer.
items.explanation: Patrick White's 1957 classic novel Voss is based on the historic 1848 inland Australian expedition led by the German explorer and naturalist Ludwig Leichhardt.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q25
items.stem:
Chronologically arrange the novels of Salman Rushdie in order of publication.
A. Fury
B. Midnight’s Children
C. The Ground Beneath Her Feet
D. The Moor’s Last Sigh
E. Grimus
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie's novels appeared in the following chronological sequence: Grimus (1975, E), Midnight's Children (1981, B), The Moor's Last Sigh (1995, D), The Ground Beneath Her Feet (1999, C), and Fury (2001, A), which establishes the order E-B-D-C-A.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q26
items.stem: Charles Lamb used the pseudonym Elia for writing in which of the following periodicals?
items.explanation: Romantic essayist Charles Lamb adopted the persona and pseudonym 'Elia' (borrowed from an Italian clerk at the South-Sea House) for his personal essays contributed to the London Magazine beginning in August 1820.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q27
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :— Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A) : The Primary component in novelistic forms is a plot that evolves coherently from its beginning to an end in which all complications are resolved.
Reason (R) : The novel is constituted by a multiplicity of divergent and contending social voices that achieve their full significance only in the process of their dialogic interaction both with each other and with the voice of the narrator.
In the light of the above two statements choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
items.explanation: Assertion (A) is false because novelistic forms are not defined simply by a closed, fully resolved plot. Reason (R) is true and states Mikhail Bakhtin's concept of 'heteroglossia' and dialogism, whereby the novel is shaped by competing social voices interacting with the narrator.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q28
items.stem:
Which among the following novels
is
not
written
by
Margaret
Atwood ?
items.explanation: Surfacing (1972), The Handmaid's Tale (1985), and The Blind Assassin (2000) are novels by Margaret Atwood, whereas The Stone Angel (1964)—the first book in the Manawaka series featuring Hagar Shipley—was written by Canadian novelist Margaret Laurence.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q29
items.stem:
Which of the following stories deal with the theme of partition?
A. Thanda Gosht
B. Gharwali
C. Jila-Watan
D. Lajwanti
E. Rudali
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: Saadat Hasan Manto's 'Thanda Gosht' (A), 'Jila-Watan' (C, Exile), and Rajinder Singh Bedi's 'Lajwanti' (D, about the rehabilitation of abducted women) are classic short stories about the 1947 Partition of India, whereas Ismat Chughtai's 'Gharwali' and Mahasweta Devi's 'Rudali' do not deal with Partition; thus A, C and D only.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q30
items.stem: Christopher Marlowe's Hero and Leander can be classified as a/an
items.explanation: Christopher Marlowe's mythological erotic poem Hero and Leander (published posthumously in 1598) is a classic Elizabethan epyllion ('little epic')—a brief narrative poem in the Ovidian tradition dealing with classical love and metamorphosis.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the List-I with List-II
List I (Cultural Critic/Theorist):
A. Raymond Williams
B. Herbert Marcuse
C. Fredric Jameson
D. Richard Hoggart

List II (Work):
I. Postmodernism, or the Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism
II. Preface to Film
III. One Dimensional Man
IV. The Uses of Literacy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The cultural theorists match their books as follows: Raymond Williams co-authored Preface to Film with Michael Orrom (A-II, 1954), Herbert Marcuse wrote One-Dimensional Man (B-III, 1964), Fredric Jameson wrote Postmodernism, or, The Cultural Logic of Late Capitalism (C-I, 1991), and Richard Hoggart wrote The Uses of Literacy (D-IV, 1957).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q32
items.stem:
“ow all their plays be neither right tragedies, nor right comedies, mingling kings and clowns,
not because the matter so carrieth it, but thrust in the clown by head and shoulders to play a
part in majestical matters”.
What term does Philip Sidney use to characterize such plays and which of the unities of
Aristotle do they violate ?
items.explanation: In An Apology for Poetry (1595), Sir Philip Sidney condemns Renaissance playwrights who produce 'mongrel tragicomedy' by indiscriminately mixing kings and clowns, thereby violating the classical Aristotelian unity of action.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q33
items.stem:
Which of the following statements are true in the context of Henry Fielding's Tom Jones (1749):
A. Tom Jones is comic and moralistic.
B. Tom and Jones are the main characters of Tom Jones.
C. Tom is caught poaching in neighbor's game preserve.
D. The History of Tom Jones is the full title of Tom Jones.
E. All of the above.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, C and D only
items.explanation: Henry Fielding's The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling (1749, D) is a comic and moralistic novel (A) in which young Tom is caught poaching on Squire Western's estate alongside gamekeeper Black George (C), whereas B falsely splits Tom Jones into two people (A, C and D only).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q34
items.stem: Whose poetry is redolent of the Orissa scene and the Jagannatha temple at Puri figures quite often in it?
items.explanation: Jayanta Mahapatra's poetry is deeply rooted in the landscape and cultural memory of Odisha, with the Jagannatha temple at Puri figuring prominently in poems such as 'Dawn at Puri' and Relationship (1980).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following works of Joseph Conrad in the chronological order of their publication :
(A) Heart of Darkness
(B) Typhoon
(C) Under Western Eyes
(D) The Nigger of the Narcissus
(E) Outcast of the Islands
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Conrad's Outcast of the Islands (1896), The Nigger of the Narcissus (1897), Heart of Darkness (1899), Typhoon (1902) and Under Western Eyes (1911) give E, D, A, B, C.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q36
items.stem: Which among the following does not fall in the category of Morality Plays?
items.explanation: The City Heiress (1682) is a Restoration comedy of manners written by Aphra Behn. The Castle of Perseverance, Mind, Will and Understanding (also called Wisdom), and Mankind are the three famous 15th-century medieval English morality plays preserved in the Macro Manuscript.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The term "Negative Capability" was coined by John Keats.
Statement II: While analysing the term "Dissociation of sensibility", T. S. Eliot proclaims that Hamlet is an artistic failure.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
items.explanation: John Keats coined 'Negative Capability' in his 21 December 1817 letter to his brothers George and Tom Keats (Statement I is true). However, T. S. Eliot called Hamlet an 'artistic failure' when discussing the 'objective correlative' in 'Hamlet and His Problems' (1919), whereas 'dissociation of sensibility' was introduced in 'The Metaphysical Poets' (1921) (Statement II is false).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q38
items.stem: Uttararamacharita by _____ is based on Valmiki's Ramayana.
items.explanation: Eighth-century Sanskrit dramatist Bhavabhuti authored the seven-act play Uttararamacharita ('The Later Story of Rama'), dramatizing the final book (Uttara Kanda) of Valmiki's Ramayana from Sita's banishment to her reunion with Rama.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q39
items.stem:
Which of the following can be classified as Science Fiction ?
(A) The Moonlight
(B) Time Machine
(C) Great Expectations
(D) The Golden Gate
(E) Brave New World
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: H. G. Wells's The Time Machine (1895, B) and Aldous Huxley's dystopian novel Brave New World (1932, E) are classic works of science fiction, making (B) and (E) Only correct.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q40
items.stem:
In which of Philip Larkin’s poem does he refer to “long uneven lines” of men waiting to be
enlisted for the war ?
(“Never such innocence again” concludes the poem)
items.explanation: In 'MCMXIV' (The Whitsun Weddings, 1964), Philip Larkin gazes at archival photographs of August 1914 enlistment volunteers outside cricket grounds ('Those long uneven lines / Standing as patiently...'), concluding memorably 'Never such innocence again.'

items.title: Mock #01 · Q41
items.stem:
Match List I with List II
List I
List II
(Writer)                                      (Book)
A. Bankimchandra Chatterjee
I. Untouchable
B. Mulk Raj Anand
II. Rajmohan's Wife
C. Panchkouree Khan
III. Stories from Indian Christian Life
D. Kamala Sathianadhan
IV. The Revelations of an Orderly
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - IV, B - I, C - II, D - III
A - I, B - III, C - II, D - IV
A - III, B - IV, C - II, D - I
A - II, B - I, C - IV, D - III
items.explanation: Bankimchandra Chatterjee wrote Rajmohan's Wife (1864, A-II), Mulk Raj Anand wrote Untouchable (1935, B-I), Panchkouree Khan wrote The Revelations of an Orderly (1848, C-IV), and Kamala Satthianadhan co-authored Stories of Indian Christian Life (1898, D-III).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q42
items.stem: Which of the following books carried the additional title Sermon on the Sea?
options: The Religion of Man by Tagore
Essay on the Gita by Aurobindo
Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule by Gandhi
items.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi's Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule (written in 1909 aboard the ship Kildonan Castle from London to South Africa) was published in an American edition in 1924 by Haridas T. Muzumdar under the title Sermon on the Sea.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q43
items.stem:
Which of the following stylistic features characterise spoken discourse?
(a) Greater use of explicit connectives
(b) Greater dependence on non-verbal connectives
(c) Greater syntactic embedding
(d) Greater use of fillers and repetitions
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: Unlike formal written prose, spontaneous spoken discourse relies heavily on non-verbal cues, intonation, and gestures rather than explicit syntactic subordination (b), and frequently features conversational fillers, pauses, and repetitions (d).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q44
items.stem:
The phrase 'Only Connect' is
associated with
items.explanation: 'Only connect!' is the famous epigraph and central humanistic motto of E. M. Forster's novel Howards End (1910), urging the reconciliation of the 'prose and the passion' of human life.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the works of Thomas Carlyle in the chronological order of publication :
(A) Periods of European Culture
(B) Specimens of German Romance
(C) Heroes and Hero Worship
(D) German Literature
(E) Revolution of Modern Europe
items.explanation: The chronological order of Thomas Carlyle's works is Specimens of German Romance (1827), German Literature (1827 essays), Periods of European Culture (1838 lectures), Revolutions of Modern Europe (1839 lectures), and On Heroes, Hero-Worship, and the Heroic in History (1841).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q46
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories and Pedagogy
items.stem: The Grammar Translation Method was historically used in teaching
items.explanation: The Grammar Translation Method was historically developed in European schools during the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries for teaching classical literature in Greek and Latin through explicit grammatical rules and direct bilingual translation.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q47
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: "...he who discovers no God whatever, how shall he discover Heroes, the visible Temples of God" is a statement by Thomas Carlyle.
Statement II: "It is not that men are ill fed, but that they have no pleasure in the work by which they make their bread, and therefore look to wealth as the only means of pleasure" is a statement made by John Ruskin.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
items.explanation: Statement I is a quotation from Thomas Carlyle's Sartor Resartus / On Heroes, Hero-Worship, and the Heroic in History, and Statement II is from John Ruskin's 'The Nature of Gothic' in The Stones of Venice (1853), critiquing alienated industrial labor (Both statements are true).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q48
items.stem: Under the Net (1954) is written by
items.explanation: Under the Net (1954) is the debut novel of Anglo-Irish philosopher and novelist Iris Murdoch, following struggling writer Jake Donaghue through picaresque and philosophical adventures across London and Paris.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q49
items.stem:
Which of these graphic narratives depict political crisis?
A. Amruta Patil - Kari
B. Joe Sacco - Footnotes in Gaza
C. Art Spiegelman - Maus
D. Sarnath Banerjee - Corridor
E. Phoebe Gloeckner - The Diary of a Teenage Girl
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Among the listed graphic narratives, Joe Sacco's Footnotes in Gaza (2009, B), investigating the 1956 killings of Palestinians in Khan Younis and Rafah, and Art Spiegelman's Maus (1980–1991, C), depicting the Nazi Holocaust, directly chronicle major political crises.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q50
items.stem: How did Chaucer's Pardoner make his living ?
options: By selling stolen cattle from the neighbourhood ottery
By assisting the Friar in Church services
By pardoning those who stole property or committed other crimes
By selling indulgences to those who committed sins
items.explanation: In Geoffrey Chaucer's The Canterbury Tales, the corrupt Pardoner earns a lucrative living by preaching on the sin of avarice ("Radix malorum est Cupiditas") while selling papal indulgences and fake holy relics to gullible sinners.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q51
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Authors)
(A) Christopher Middleton
(B) Patricia Waugh
(C) David Kennedy
(D) Edward Larrissy

List II (Critical Works)
(I) Poem Relations: The Refashioning of British Poetry 1980-1994
(II) Distant Reading: Performance, Readership, and Consumption in Contemporary Poetry
(III) Reading Twentieth-Century Poetry: The Language of Expression
(IV) The Harvest of the Sixties: English Literature and Its Background 1960-1990

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Christopher Middleton wrote Distant Reading (A-II); Patricia Waugh authored The Harvest of the Sixties: English Literature and Its Background 1960–1990 (B-IV); David Kennedy authored Poem Relations (C-I); and Edward Larrissy wrote Reading Twentieth-Century Poetry (D-III).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q52
items.stem:
Coleridge's
"The
Rime
of
the
Ancient Mariner" is a poem in
_________
items.explanation: Samuel Taylor Coleridge's ballad "The Rime of the Ancient Mariner," first published as the opening poem of Lyrical Ballads (1798), is divided into seven distinct parts.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q53
items.stem:
Which two of the following essays have proved particularly productive in the disciplinary practices of Cultural Studies?
(A) Laura Mulvey, “Visual Pleasure and Narrative Cinema”
(B) Viktor Shklovsky, “Art as Technique”
(C) Sigmund Freud, “The Uncanny”
(D) Stuart Hall, “Encoding/decoding”
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
items.explanation: Mulvey's essay on the male gaze and Hall's encoding/decoding model have been central to Cultural Studies.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q54
items.stem: What is register ?
options: The way in which a language registers in the minds of its users.
The way users of a language register the nuances of that language.
A variety of language used in non-professional or informal situations by professionals.
A variety of language used in social situations or one specially designed for the subject it deals with.
items.explanation: In sociolinguistics and stylistics, 'register' refers to a variety of language defined according to its use in specific social situations, occupational contexts, or subject fields (such as legal, scientific, or journalistic register).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q55
items.stem:
What is the correct chronological order of the publication of the following?
(a) German Grammar (Jacob Grimm)
(b) Comparative Grammar of Sanskrit, Zend, Greek, Latin, Lithuanian, Gothic and German (Franz Bopp)
(c) An Investigation into the Origin of Old Norse or Icelandic Language (Rasmus Rask)
(d) Concerning the Conjugation System of the Sanskrit Language in Comparison with those of the Greek, Latin, Persian and German Languages (Franz Bopp)
items.explanation: Rasmus Rask completed his prize essay An Investigation into the Origin of the Old Norse or Icelandic Language in 1814 (published 1818) (c), followed by Franz Bopp's On the Conjugation System of the Sanskrit Language (1816) (d), Jacob Grimm's Deutsche Grammatik (German Grammar, 1819) (a), and Franz Bopp's Comparative Grammar (1833) (b).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q56
items.stem: Which writer of the Romantic period makes the following comment : “The poet is far from dealing only with these subtle and analogical truths. Truth of every kind belongs to him, provided it can bud into any kind of beauty, or is capable of being illustrated and impressed by poetic faculty” ?
options: Leigh Hunt in What is Poetry ?
William Hazlitt in “On the Feeling of Immortality in Youth”
Wordsworth in Preface to the Lyrical Ballads
Keats in one of his letters to his brother
items.explanation: This passage comes from Leigh Hunt's critical essay 'What is Poetry?' (published as the opening essay of Imagination and Fancy, 1844), where Hunt defines poetry as the utterance of a passion for truth, beauty, and power.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q57
items.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Hannah Arendt's "defactualization" is very close to the concept of "Post-truth".
Statement II: Post-truth relies on absolute lies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
items.explanation: In 'Lying in Politics' (1971), Hannah Arendt introduced the concept of 'defactualization'—the systemic erosion of the distinction between factual truth and opinion—which closely anticipates the modern concept of 'post-truth' (Statement I is correct). However, post-truth does not rely simply on absolute lies, but on emotional appeals, half-truths, and ideological belief superseding objective facts (Statement II is incorrect).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q58
items.stem: Who is the author of the short story, The Ghost of Firozsha Baag?
items.explanation: 'The Ghost of Firozsha Baag' is a story in Rohinton Mistry's collection 'Tales from Firozsha Baag' (1987).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q59
items.stem:
Which of the two following books are written by Dipesh Chakrabarty?
A. Provincializing Europe: Postcolonial Thought and Historical Difference
B. The Subaltern Studies Reader
C. Identity and Violence
D. The Climate of History in a Planetary Age
E. In Other Worlds
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Historian and postcolonial theorist Dipesh Chakrabarty authored Provincializing Europe: Postcolonial Thought and Historical Difference (2000, A) and The Climate of History in a Planetary Age (2021, D). The Subaltern Studies Reader was edited by Ranajit Guha, Identity and Violence is by Amartya Sen, and In Other Worlds is by Gayatri Chakravorty Spivak.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q60
items.stem: Who is the author of "A Fragment" (1819), one of the earliest vampire stories in English?
items.explanation: Lord Byron composed the unfinished prose tale 'A Fragment' (centering on the mysterious aristocrat Augustus Darvell dying in the ruins of Ephesus) during the famous ghost-story contest at the Villa Diodati in June 1816. Byron published it alongside Mazeppa in 1819, and his physician John Polidori expanded its premise into The Vampyre (1819).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q61
items.stem:
Match the column:
(Poet)
A. Edmund Spenser
B. Philip Sidney
C. Thomas Wyatt
D. Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey
(poem)
I. “Whoso List to Hunt”
II. “So Cruel Prison how could Betide”
III. “The Faerie Queene”
IV. “The Defense of Poesy”
items.explanation: Edmund Spenser composed the epic allegorical poem The Faerie Queene (1590) (A-III); Philip Sidney wrote the critical treatise The Defense of Poesy (published 1595) (B-IV); Sir Thomas Wyatt wrote the Petrarchan sonnet adaptation "Whoso List to Hunt" (C-I); and Henry Howard, Earl of Surrey, composed the reflective Windsor elegy "So Cruel Prison how could Betide" (D-II). This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q62
items.stem: Who among the following is the author of Steps to the Temple ?
items.explanation: Metaphysical poet Richard Crashaw wrote Steps to the Temple. Sacred Poems, With other Delights of the Muses (1646), whose title pays homage to George Herbert's devotional collection The Temple (1633).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q63
items.stem:
Which among the following are false in the context of autographical research?
A. These can be accepted on face value.
B. These are usually idealized.
C. These are coloured by compelling motive of the desire for self-justification.
D. These are embroidered through the sheer exuberance of the artistic imagination.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Richard D. Altick's The Art of Literary Research, autobiographical sources cannot be accepted at face value (making A false) precisely because they are usually idealized (B), coloured by a motive of self-justification (C), and embroidered by artistic imagination (D); Option 2 (B, C and D only) groups the three true reasons why autobiographical accounts are unreliable at face value.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q64
items.stem:
"The City of Dreadful Night", a long
poem depicting the late Victorian
sense of gloom and despondency, is
written by
items.explanation: 'The City of Dreadful Night' (1874) was written by Scottish-born Victorian poet James Thomson under the pseudonym 'B.V.' (Bysshe Vanolis). The bleak, pessimistic poem portrays a nightmare metropolis of urban alienation and existential despair.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q65
items.stem: What is the correct chronological order of publication of the texts given under? (A) R.K. Narayan's The Financial Expert (B) Manohar Malgonkar's A Bend in the Ganges (C) Raja Rao's Kanthapura (D) Shashi Tharoor's The Great Indian Novel (E) Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological publication sequence is: Raja Rao's Kanthapura (1938), R.K. Narayan's The Financial Expert (1952), Manohar Malgonkar's A Bend in the Ganges (1964), Shashi Tharoor's The Great Indian Novel (1989), and Arundhati Roy's The God of Small Things (1997) [(C), (A), (B), (D), (E)].

items.title: Mock #01 · Q66
items.stem:
Who amongst the following is not a
Jewish-American novelist ?
items.explanation: William Faulkner was a Southern American modernist writer from Mississippi, celebrated for his Yoknapatawpha County novels rather than Jewish-American fiction, whereas Philip Roth and J. D. Salinger are major American writers of Jewish heritage.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q67
items.meta: Unit V: Language: Basic Concepts, Theories & Pedagogy
items.stem:
Which of the following points are correct regarding the Direct Method of teaching English in a classroom scenario?

A. There is no interference of the mother tongue.
B. There is direct connection with the target language (English). Learners think in the target language and express in the target language.
C. The teaching learning process is carried out in English.
D. This method is useful in overcrowded classroom situation.
E. This method is based on the principle of ‘Doing by Learning.’

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The Direct Method of language teaching bans mother-tongue translation (A), fosters direct cognitive association with the target language (B), and conducts all instruction strictly in English (C); it requires small groups with extensive personal interaction and is unsuited to overcrowded classrooms.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q68
items.stem: Virginia Woolf borrowed the idea of the common reader from Dr. Johnson. To which particular work of Johnson's does she remain indebted ?
options: The Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets; the essay on Milton
The Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets; the essay on Gray
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf took the title and epigraph of The Common Reader (1925) from Samuel Johnson's 'Life of Gray' in The Lives of the Most Eminent English Poets (1779–1781), where Johnson praises Gray's Elegy by declaring, 'I rejoice to concur with the common reader.'

items.title: Mock #01 · Q69
items.stem:

options: A - II, B - I, C - IV, D - III
A - I, B - IV, C - III, D - II
A - IV, B - III, C - II, D - I
A - III, B - IV, C - I, D - II
items.explanation: Doll Common is the con-woman accomplice in Ben Jonson's The Alchemist (1610, A-II), Malvolio is Olivia's puritanical steward in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night (B-I), Roger Mortimer is the antagonist in Marlowe's Edward II (C-IV), and Bosola is the malcontent spy in Webster's The Duchess of Malfi (D-III).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q70
items.stem: Who among the following translated Aristotle's Poetics in Latin?
items.explanation: Italian humanist Giorgio Valla published the first printed Latin translation of Aristotle's Poetics in Venice in 1498, an intellectual milestone that initiated Renaissance European critical debate on tragedy and mimesis.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q71
items.stem:
Which two writers have written essays on the defence of poetry?
(a) Sir Philip Sidney
(b) P.B. Shelley
(c) Dr. Mathew Arnold
(d) T.S. Eliot
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: Sidney wrote 'An Apology for Poetry' and Shelley wrote 'A Defence of Poetry'.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q72
items.stem: Which two cities are referred in Charles Dickens' A Tale of Two Cities?
items.explanation: Set against the violent upheaval of the French Revolution, Charles Dickens's historical novel A Tale of Two Cities (1859) explicitly contrasts London and Paris through the intertwined fates of Charles Darnay and Sydney Carton.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q73
items.stem:
Arrange the following essays in the chronological order of publication.
 A. T. S. Eliot, "The Function of Criticism"
 B. Edgar Allan Poe, "The Philosophy of Composition"
 C. Henry James, "The Art of Fiction"

 D. Virginia Woolf, "Modern Fiction"
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The chronological sequence of these critical essays is Edgar Allan Poe's 'The Philosophy of Composition' (1846, B), Henry James's 'The Art of Fiction' (1884, C), Virginia Woolf's 'Modern Fiction' (1919, D), and T.S. Eliot's 'The Function of Criticism' (1923, A).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q74
items.stem: Who among the following is the recipient of Nobel Prize in Literature for the year 2021?
items.explanation: Tanzanian-born British novelist Abdulrazak Gurnah, author of celebrated novels such as Paradise (1994) and By the Sea (2001), was awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in Literature for his compassionate exploration of the effects of colonialism and the fate of refugees.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q75
items.stem:
Identify the plays originally written by Vijay Tendulkar from the following:
A. The Cyclist and His Fifth Woman
B. Scandal in Fairyland
C. The Vultures and Encounter in Umbugland
D. Sakharam Binder
E. Fire and the Rain
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: Marathi playwright Vijay Tendulkar wrote The Cyclist (Safar, 1991), His Fifth Woman (2004) (A), The Vultures (Gidhade, 1970), Encounter in Umbugland (Dambadwipcha Mukabala, 1968) (C), and Sakharam Binder (1972) (D), whereas Scandal in Fairyland is by Badal Sircar and The Fire and the Rain is by Girish Karnad.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q76
items.stem: Literary works such as Charles Dickens's David Copperfield, Samuel Butler's The Way of All Flesh and James Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man provide examples of which following novelistic form ?
items.explanation: Charles Dickens's David Copperfield (1850), Samuel Butler's The Way of All Flesh (1903), and James Joyce's A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man (1916) are all classic examples of the Bildungsroman (novel of formation or education), tracing a protagonist's growth from childhood to maturity.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q77
items.stem:

(IV) Thomas Betterton

(2) The 18th century
(3) The Restoration
(4) The 20th century

Codes : (I) (II) (III) (IV)
items.explanation: David Garrick was the premier Shakespearean actor-manager of the 18th century (2), John Gielgud dominated the 20th-century stage (4), Sir Henry Irving was the celebrated Victorian/19th-century actor (1), and Thomas Betterton was the leading actor of the Restoration stage (3).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q78
items.stem: Who is of the opinion that the concept of “ideology” is “the most important conceptual category in cultural studies”?
items.explanation: Graeme Turner asserts in *British Cultural Studies: An Introduction* (1990) that 'ideology is the most important conceptual category in cultural studies,' central to analyzing how cultural texts produce social meaning and sustain power hierarchies.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q79

Choose the correct answers from the options given below:
options: A, D, C, D and E
E, C, D, A and B
B, D, A, E and C
C, B, A, E and D
items.explanation: The chronological order of publication of these dramatic criticism books is: Eric Bentley's The Playwright as Thinker (1946, C), Martin Esslin's The Theatre of the Absurd (1961, B), Robert Brustein's The Theatre of Revolt (1964, A), J.L. Styan's Modern Drama in Theory and Practice (1981, E), and C.W.E. Bigsby's Modern American Drama (1992, D).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q80
items.stem: "She dwells with beauty - Beauty that must die", - wrote Keats in one of his odes, referring to
items.explanation: This famous line opens the final stanza of John Keats's 'Ode on Melancholy' (1819), in which Keats personifies Melancholy ('She') as inseparable from transient earthly Beauty and fleeting Joy.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q81
items.stem:

(c) Interventions / (iii) Feminist writing
(d) Signs / (iv) Postcolonial writing
Choose the correct option from those given below :
items.explanation: Obsidian covers African diaspora arts, Clio covers literature and history, Interventions is postcolonial and Signs is feminist.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q82
items.stem: In Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress which of the following are found in the Slough of Despond?
options: Hope, great expectations, and dreams of the future.
Fears and doubts, discouraging apprehensions, sinful thoughts.
items.explanation: In John Bunyan's The Pilgrim's Progress (1678), Help explains that the Slough of Despond cannot be mended because all the fears, doubts, discouraging apprehensions, and sinful anxieties that accompany the conviction of sin continually settle into this mire.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q83
items.stem:

A. The Trumpet Major
B. The Hand of Ethelberta

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological publication order of Thomas Hardy's novels is: The Hand of Ethelberta (1876, B), The Return of the Native (1878, E), The Trumpet-Major (1880, A), The Woodlanders (1887, D), and Tess of the d'Urbervilles (1891, C).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q84

items.explanation: Poetry composed without a fixed metrical foot, regular rhyme scheme, or prescribed stanzaic pattern is known both as 'free verse' (vers libre, III) and 'open form' (I), whereas blank verse (IV) has a strict meter (unrhymed iambic pentameter).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q86
items.stem:

options: Wilfred Owen, Siegfried Sassoon, Rupert Brooke

Auden, Louis MacNeice, Cecil Day Lewis

items.explanation: Hugo Gernsback pioneered early science fiction literature and magazine publishing (A-III); Edmund Husserl founded the philosophical discipline of phenomenology (B-II); John Crowe Ransom established American New Criticism with his 1941 book (C-IV); and Michel Foucault developed the critical theory of biopolitics (D-I).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q88
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of the ideal state in Thomas More's Utopia ?
options: Personal property, money and vice are effectively abolished
The root causes of crime, ambition and political conflict, are eliminated

items.explanation: In Book II of Thomas More's Utopia (1516), Utopians do not have only one single religion; instead, various religions coexist peacefully across the island and within each city under King Utopus's policy of religious toleration.

Romantic essayist Charles Lamb wrote 'On the Artificial Comedy of the Last Century' (in Essays of Elia, 1823), and Jonathan Swift published the satirical pamphlet 'A Modest Proposal' (1729).

items.title: Mock #01 · Q91
items.stem:
Read the following piece of poetry and answer the questions from 91 to 95.

When I was fair and young, then favor graced me,
Of many was I sought their mistress for to be,
But I did scorn them all and answered them therefore:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

How many weeping eyes I made to pine in woe,
How many sighing hearts I have not skill to show,
But I the prouder grew and still this spake therefore:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

Then spake fair Venus' son, that proud victorious boy,
Saying: you dainty dame, for that you be so coy,
I will so pluck your plumes as you shall say no more:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

As soon as he had said such change grew in my breast,
That neither night nor day I could take any rest,
Wherefore I did repent that I had said before:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

Question 91: What does the line, "When I was fair and young, then favor graced me", appear to connote?
options: She was very beautiful and young
The lady had good fortune and was wealthy
She had the favour of many of her lovers
items.explanation: In the opening line of Queen Elizabeth I's lyric 'When I Was Fair and Young', 'fair and young' and 'favor graced me' connote that the speaker was blessed with youth, physical beauty, and comeliness that attracted many admirers.

When I was fair and young, then favor graced me,
Of many was I sought their mistress for to be,
But I did scorn them all and answered them therefore:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

How many weeping eyes I made to pine in woe,
How many sighing hearts I have not skill to show,
But I the prouder grew and still this spake therefore:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

Then spake fair Venus' son, that proud victorious boy,
Saying: you dainty dame, for that you be so coy,
I will so pluck your plumes as you shall say no more:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

As soon as he had said such change grew in my breast,
That neither night nor day I could take any rest,
Wherefore I did repent that I had said before:
Go, go, go, seek some other where, importune me no more.

Question 95: What did the lady repent for?
options: For breaking the heart of so many of her lovers
For her rudeness and false pride
For not responding her last lover
For not caring the feelings of others
items.explanation: After Cupid strikes her breast with unrequited longing so that she can take no rest day or night, the speaker repents of her earlier rudeness, false pride, and scornful dismissal of her suitors.

items.title: Mock #01 · Q96
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the following passage and answer the questions.

There is nothing that more betrays a base ungenerous spirit than the giving of secret stabs to a man's reputation; lampoons and satires that are written with wit and spirit are like poisoned darts, which not only inflict a wound, but make it incurable. For this reason I am very much troubled when I see the talents of humour and ridicule in the possession of an ill-natured man. There cannot be a greater gratification to a barbarous and inhuman wit than to stir up sorrow in the heart of a private person, to raise uneasiness among near relations, and to expose whole families to derision, at the same time that he remains unseen and undiscovered. If, besides the accomplishments of being witty and ill-natured, a man is vicious into the bargain, he is one of the most mischievous creatures that can enter into a civil society. His satire will then chiefly fall upon those who ought to be the most exempt from it. Virtue, merit, and everything, that is praiseworthy, will be made the subject of ridicule and buffoonery. It is impossible to enumerate the evils which arise from these arrow that fly in the dark; and I know no other excuse that is or can be made for them, than that the wounds they give are only imaginary, and produce nothing more than a secret shame or sorrow in the mind of the suffering person.

Question 96: In the passage, "secret stabs" stands for:
options: Poisoned darts which pricks and inflicts
items.explanation: In this passage from Joseph Addison's The Spectator (No. 23), 'the giving of secret stabs to a man's reputation' refers directly to malicious 'lampoons and satires that are written with wit and spirit' to wound a person covertly.
